standard: Field Assembly Record Standard 1.2, §8 market records; see PROVENANCE.md
notes: DRAFT, not reviewed and not signed. Prose drafted 2026-11-16 by a session from numbers.md and numbers.json of run 2026-11-16T134103Z, modeled on Issue 1. One drafting pass and one run of tools/check.py, which passes at 120 figures. No figure in the prose is absent from numbers.json. What was recalculated from the retained captures rather than from numbers.json, all matching. BLS, the five per-series JSON files of the issue run: chicken eggs PPI 82.889 (2026-10, preliminary) against 323.307 (2025-10) gives -74.4%, against 404.269 (2024-10) -79.5%, against the 1302.339 peak of 2025-02 -93.6%; butter PPI 95.664 against 117.897 gives -18.9% and against 189.115 -49.4%; the three CPI series carry '-' for 2025 M10 with footnote X, 'Data unavailable due to the 2025 lapse in appropriations', and their two-year figures (-16.2%, -10.6%, +7.6%) recompute. Report 2848, issue-run PDF dated Fri Nov 13, 2026 for 11/08-11/14: national delivered warehouse Large 99.19, last reported 80.19; Midwest paid to producers FOB Large 71.00, last reported 52.00; Northeast delivered warehouse Large 100.00, last reported 81.00; the four-week averages 76.94, 48.75 and 77.75 recompute from the PDFs of the 10-23, 10-31, 11-06 and 11-13 runs. NDPSR butter.json of the issue run, each week at its latest restatement: 1.3560 and 3,366,906 lb for 11/07/2026; 1.6627 and 3,422,150 lb for 11/08/2025 (first published 1.6616 and 3,418,625); four-week averages 1.362925 and 1.69765; -18.4%, -19.7%, -1.6%, +8.9%. Dairy Market News page 1: weekly average 1.2895 (11/6), 1.3145 (10/30), Friday close 1.2650, -1.9%. NASS ckeg1026.txt: average layers 385,065 against 368,338 (+4.5%), table eggs 7,931.6 against 7,448.6 (+6.5%). ERS CSV: the four egg and dairy attributes quoted. Bare counts and worded quantities checked by hand, since the gate reads none of them: nine weeks of report 2848 in the record (weeks ending 2026-09-19 to 2026-11-14) and eight weeks of the CME reprint (2026-09-18 to 2026-11-06), both counted in data/indicators.jsonl and against the PDFs; seven Large white markets in report 2848, three reported, and all seven higher than the prior week; each of the three reported markets at the highest of its nine weeks; the weekly paths quoted for the three markets; eleven earlier runs behind the accumulated series; BLS marking four months (2026 M07 to M10) preliminary; 'two weeks into November'; 64.19 'three weeks before' 11-14 (week ending 10-24); the statement that the butter PPI is lower in October than in September (95.664 against 100.431 in the same file), given as a direction only because month-to-month is not in the computed set; the statement that the year-over-year butter falls are smaller than Issue 1 reported and that the October 2025 base is below the September 2025 base (117.897 against 147.657); the product specifications and the report 2848 note 'Prices to retailers, sales to volume buyers, white eggs in cartons', read from the captures. Comparisons that do not exist and are named in the prose: year-over-year for CPI eggs, CPI butter and CPI food away from home (BLS lapse); year-over-year for the three shell egg markets, single week and four-week average (nine weeks in the record); year-over-year for the CME reprint (eight weeks); two-year for the two NASS series (no 2024-09 reading). evidence.json was checked and not edited: it lists the report 2848 and Dairy Market News captures of all eleven earlier runs and every capture of the issue run; the NASS 'txt' fetch is listed SKIPPED because the archive file was fetched. Open points for the editor. 1. The CME reading is stale by a week: the Dairy Market News URL served Volume 93 Report 45 (week of November 2-6, Last-Modified November 6) on both the 11-13 and 11-16 runs, so the record has no week ending 2026-11-13; the issue says so. 2. Source restatements touching Issue 1, verified in the captures but absent from this issue's numbers.json and therefore not quoted: NDPSR week ending 2026-10-10 is now 1.3658 and 3,174,076 lb where Issue 1 reported the first-published 1.3600 and 2,780,060 lb, which turns Issue 1's -11.3% volume comparison into a small increase against 3,135,144 lb; NASS August 2026 is now 383,405 thousand layers and 8,146.3 million table eggs where Issue 1 reported 382,801 and 8,121.6. The issue describes both without figures; whether Issue 1 gets a note under the corrections rule in methodology.md, and whether issue.py should carry restated prior-issue figures, is the editor's decision. 3. methodology.md and sources.json describe the national delivered warehouse price as what a distributor pays; the report's own note says prices to retailers, sales to volume buyers. The issue uses the report's wording. 4. The week-on-week changes the report itself prints (19.00 cents this week, 16.00 the week before) are not in numbers.json and are not quoted. 5. The first-published and restated figures the methodology says an issue notes when they differ (week ending 10-17 restated to 1.3630 from 1.3547; prior-year week 1.6627 from 1.6616) are not in numbers.json, so the issue notes the restatement without the first-published figure. 6. The header date is the run date, 2026-11-16, and should become the publication date. 7. The Next issue line carries no date: no retained capture states the BLS release date for November indexes. 8. The butter sales rows are in numbers.json but not in numbers.md; the issue table includes them as Issue 1 did, plus the four-week sales average and the Northeast four-week average. 9. The task brief referred to a bls series.json capture; the run retains five per-series JSON files and capture.json, and those were what was read. 10. The egg PPI for October is preliminary and the weekly quotations rose sharply in the two following weeks; the issue reports both and states no cause. The Egg Markets Overview was not read for one. Independent review 2026-11-16 (a separate session pass that recalculated every headline figure, date, weekday and count from the captures; all matched numbers.json; all 37 evidence.json hashes re-checked). Applied: 'Butter is lower on the year on every measure' corrected, since the four-week average of qualifying pounds is 8.9% higher; the read and the buyer's question no longer set the October egg index's fall on the year beside the November quotations' week-on-week rise as one thing moving 'the other way' or 'measured at' two dates; 'across the month of October' made 'with October 2026 as its reference month' (no retained file says the index averages the month); the BLS statement narrowed to the three consumer price series this record holds; the restatement paragraph now says figures from two sources, and names the week ending October 3 (1.3696 and 5,395,605 lb as Issue 1 used; now 1.3641 and 5,401,172 lb) as well as October 10 (1.3600 and 2,780,060 lb; now 1.3658 and 3,174,076 lb, against 3,135,144 lb a year earlier); the NASS revision sentence says where the earlier release is retained (run 2026-10-18T144956Z: 382,801 and 8,121.6; now 383,405 and 8,146.3), because this issue's evidence.json does not list it; the butter 'not evidence' sentence limited to the producer index; smaller wording points on the four-week averages, the supplier sentence and 'As in October'. Left for the editor: methodology.md says an issue notes the first-published figure when it differs, which this draft cannot do for 1.6616 (now 1.6627, week ending 11/08/2025) or 1.3547 (now 1.3630, 10/17/2026) because they are not in numbers.json; methodology.md and sources.json call the national delivered warehouse price 'what a distributor pays' where the report says 'Prices to retailers, sales to volume buyers, white eggs in cartons'; Issue 1's printed '11.3% below' for butter volume is reversed by the restatement, and whether it gets an appended note is the editor's decision; Dairy Market News Report 44 prints the 10/30 weekly average as '(+0.0345)' where the record's prior week makes it a fall of 0.0345 (no quoted figure affected); the header date is the run date and becomes the publication date.
